Find the area bounded between the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{x-1}+1,$ the $y$-axis and the lines $y=0$ and $y=1,$ as shown above.
worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{x-1}+1 \\ y-1 & =\sqrt[3]{x-1} \\ (y-1)^{3} & =x-1 \\ x & =(y-1)^{3}+1 \\ x & ={y}^{3}-3{y}^{2}+3y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{3}-3{y}^{2}+3y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y-3{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y+3{\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}-3\cdot {\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}+3\cdot {\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}-0)-3(\frac{1}{3}-0)+3(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-1+\frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
